rationale: A CLASS `implements` clause written with TYPE ARGUMENTS must publish the BASE NAME. tree-sitter-typescript 0.23.2 produces arguments as a sibling `type_arguments` node for BOTH class-extends shapes (`extends GenBase<string>` -> [type_identifier, type_arguments]; `extends ns.QBase<string>` -> [member_expression, type_arguments]) but as a SINGLE `generic_type` child for `implements Gen<string>` and for interface heritage. The analyzer's existing `type.type === 'type_arguments'` sibling skip therefore handled class extends and MISSED class implements, whose target kept its arguments. Three measured costs, each pinned below: (1) filterNoiseRelationships (src/ast/pool-worker.ts:654) drops any target whose leaf contains `<` or `>`, so production deleted these edges — raw-analyzer vs production on the same files: rxjs implements 51->43 (8 lost, 15.69%), nest 252->213 (39 lost, 15.48%), typeorm 158->127 (31 lost, 19.62%); all 78 losses were exactly this shape and nothing else, and all three read 0 after the fix. (2) The endpoint could not bind, since `Gen<string>` is not a declared name. (3) The structural OVERRIDE arm resolves its base by name, so `ifaceByName.get('Subscribable<T>')` never matched the declared `Subscribable` — on rxjs packages/observable-polyfill/src/index.ts that cost 6 overrides edges, 4 of which the oracle had already derived as MISSING truth, and that file went from 1 overrides edge to 7. The oracle already strips at the first `<` for every TYPE heritage node (differential.ts heritage collect, citing the same groovy `Cache<T>` case), so this restores lockstep rather than introducing a third spelling. The extends CONTROL is pinned because it was already correct via the sibling skip: a strip added there was mutant-tested, SURVIVED (no shape reaches it with arguments attached), and was removed rather than shipped untested. The nested-generic-arguments case pins that the strip cuts at the FIRST `<`.

expectRelationships.note: THE GAIN: `implements Gen<string>` published `Gen<string>` before, which production then deleted
the non-generic entry in a mixed clause is unchanged
THE GAIN: second entry of the same clause, arguments stripped
THE GAIN: generic entry on a class that also extends
the strip cuts at the FIRST `<`, so nested `Array<Map<string, number>>` arguments do not survive

CONTROL: generic `extends` is already correct because its arguments arrive as a SIBLING type_arguments node, which the sibling skip removes. A strip at this call site was mutant-tested and survived, so there is none.

THE CASCADE: the structural override arm looks its base up by name. With the base spelled `Gen<number>` it never matched, so this edge could not exist. Same mechanism that hid 6 edges on rxjs's observable-polyfill.
